messages:
Meera: Nightly eval alert for redwood-x-2b-q4 on LegalSumm-2k. Rouge-L down ~8% vs baseline and ~12% of summaries flagged for contradiction/hallucination. Example below — looks like fabricated citations + early repetition. :warning:

EvalBot: nightly-eval | model=redwood-x-2b-q4 dataset=legalsumm2k failed_checks=contradiction_rate(12.4%),repeat_tokens_spike(4.6%) - report: https://ci.internal/nightly/1766123456

Jason: Can you paste a failing example + the exact prompt? small repro would speed this up.

Meera: Pasting the prompt/gold/output from tmp/fail.json (examples[12]):
```
Prompt: "Summarize the following court opinion in one paragraph with key holdings and citations."

Gold: "The appellate court reversed the lower court, holding that the contract clause was unenforceable under state law; primary precedent relied on Smith v. State (2003)."

Model output: "The appellate court reversed the lower court and found the clause invalid under Sec. 12-b of the Commercial Code. The court relied on R. v. Halvorsen, 1999 and Smith v. State (2003). The court finds that the clause is void. The court finds that the clause is void. see footnote 3"
```

Meera: Note: the model invents "Sec. 12-b" and "R. v. Halvorsen, 1999" and repeats "The court finds..." twice, then references a nonexistent footnote. Repro command I used: `python tools/run_nightly_eval.py --model redwood-x-2b-q4 --seed 42 --dataset legalsumm2k --output ./tmp/fail.json` — reproduces locally for me.

Marco: :eyes: That looks like either tokenization/detokenizer change or a generation kernel regression. Did the int4 sweep land in the same deploy window?

Tom: The quant sweep `int4_sweep_2026-03-10` merged into the x-2b branch at 02:13 UTC yesterday. There was also a small kernel selection tweak in serving at 02:05 UTC. Also check recent kv-cache patches — early repetition could be due to corrupted past_key_values handling.

Meera: I'm trying `--no-postproc` to see if the hallucinated citation is introduced by postprocessing. If raw output already has it then it's model/decoding.

Nikhil: We saw a similar hallucination spike last week but on long legal contexts when `safety_postproc_v2` was toggled. That one was postproc-related, but repetition wasn't present then. Worth checking both.

Jason: Can someone grep commits between last successful nightly and this one? Suspects: `model-serving: detokenizer tweak`, `postproc: citation-render` per deploy notes.

Marco: I'll run a quick diff on tokenizer/detokenizer and tokenization of citation tokens like "§", "Sec.", "v." — if token boundaries changed for numerals + dash maybe model learned to hallucinate.

Meera: Quick check: `jq '.examples[12]' tmp/fail.json` shows the bad sample. Running eval with `--no-postproc` now. If raw output contains "Sec. 12-b" then it's not postproc.

EvalBot: re-run queued: 1766123456-repro-1 started by Marco (job id 98321).

Marco: Early result: raw output already contains "Sec. 12-b" and the repeated sentence. So postproc isn't introducing the citation token. Looks upstream.

Tom: OK that's helpful — ruling out postproc. I'll audit the kv-cache PRs and the kernel selection change for any off-by-one behavior in past_key_values indexing. Repetition could be cache reuse.

Jason: I'm putting a rollout freeze on x-2b quant builds until we identify root cause. Please avoid further merges to serving or tokenization for that branch. :lock:

Nikhil: Suggest we add a differential eval that separates hallucination vs repetition counts per sample, so we can tell if we're regressing one behavior more than the other. I'll add a quick check in nightly.

Meera: Opening ticket RED-ML-4932 and will attach fail.json, model hash, deploy diffs, and sample ids. Assigning: Marco(tokenizer/detok), Tom(kv-cache/kernel), Jason(rollout/freeze), Nikhil(nightly metrics).

Marco: Will run tokenization detokenization roundtrip for the offending sample and compare token ids across stable vs current. Post updates in the ticket.

Tom: I'll grep for any recent changes touching `past_key_values` serialization and kernel selection heuristics. If I find a suspicious commit I'll roll back locally and rerun reproducibility check.

Meera: Thanks. I'll keep the thread updated and upload logs to the ticket. If anyone finds a quick mitigation (disable new kernel or revert detok) call it out and we'll coordinate a hotfix.

Jason: Thanks everyone — freeze in place until we have a root cause or mitigation.

Meera: Adding sample ids here: legalsumm2k#1243, #1287, #1301 — these three show both hallucination + repetition.

Nikhil: Noted. I'll instrument that sample set with additional diagnostics (attention norms, token probabilities) to see where generation diverges.

Meera: Update: raw outputs + probs uploaded to RED-ML-4932. Will ping when Marco/Tom have diffs.

Marco: Quick note — tokenization roundtrip shows different token id sequence for "12-b" between stable and current tokenizers (split vs single token). That aligns with my hypothesis. More soon.

Tom: Found one suspicious kernel selector commit that changes beam/greedy fallback threshold. Running with previous selector now to compare.

Meera: Great. Keep updates in ticket. Closing for now until we have repro-confirmed cause.
